question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,y\le z\le y+1\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{4}[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{2z}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{4}(2z-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{y}^{y+1}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}[{z}^{2}]_{z=y}^{z=y+1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}((y+1)^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}(2y+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[{y}^{2}+y]}_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(9+3)-\frac{1}{4}(1+1) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
